summary: Deferred response timeouts on deep-context requests when server-side batching is enabled
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a pattern of streaming responses that begin normally for very long prompts (deep contexts + large max_tokens) but then stall for a prolonged period and eventually time out or result in a client connection reset. Impact: customer Draftly (Dedicated) experiences frequent content-generation failures for batch jobs that synthesize large documents, blocking workflows and causing SLA alerts.

Observed behaviour: initial tokens stream out, then a long pause (~45-90s) with no bytes emitted, followed by either 504 from edge or TCP RST observed by the customer. This occurs only when server-side batching is enabled on the route and for requests with large context + max_tokens (examples below).

Business impact: blocking for Draftly's nightly batch document generation; several failed jobs reported, customer escalated to account team.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a request to /v1/generate with model=redwood-v1-large and batching=true
Compose prompt ~28k tokens of combined system+history and request max_tokens=120000
Send request via streaming websocket or SSE client that keeps keepalive enabled
Observe initial stream chunks for first 5-10 tokens, then stall for 45-90s, then client observes RST or server returns 504
Repeat with batching disabled: request completes (very slow) but does not hit the stall pattern

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Batcher is grouping long-context requests which trigger heavy kv-prefetch and kernel work; combined with kernel swap policy this caused those requests to be preempted and queued behind other work, resulting in long stalls and edge timeouts.
Hypothesis 2: Continuous batching window logic (50ms) has a path where kv-cache locks are held into the scheduling decision, causing a dead-time when a later batch member induces a kernel swap.

Finding: Correlated events in node gpu-46 show kernel-preemption events coincident with stalled request_ids. Batcher log shows request moved to pending queue with reason=kv_prefetch_lock and wait durations matching customer-observed stall time.
Reproduction: Staging run with batching=true and context_tokens >25000 produced identical stall pattern. Disabling batching completed the same payload without the stall (long but steady throughput).
Temporary mitigation: Route override to disable batching for requests where context_tokens > 25000 or max_tokens > 80000. This reduced customer failures to zero for the observed jobs.

Root cause (provisional): Interaction between batched KV prefetch locking and kernel-swap preemption on nodes with mixed-priority workloads. When a batched request requires a kernel that causes a swap, the batcher holds the slot and waits while the node preempts; other batch members remain blocked leading to a long stall rather than fast failover to a fallback model.

Next steps: harden batcher to detect long-context members and either schedule them to isolated pools or run them unbatched; adjust kernel-swap policy to avoid preempting long-running inference kernels; add observability metric for batch-member wait time and kv-lock durations.
resolution: Workaround implemented 2026-03-06: route override to disable batching for large-context requests for Draftly's dedicated pool. This restored nightly job success while patch progressed.

Fix in progress: scheduler/batcher patch to skip batching for requests meeting large-context thresholds and to avoid holding kv-cache locks across preemption windows. PR #9821 opened and under code review. Canary rollout scheduled 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC.
Customer communication: Informed Draftly that a temporary workaround is in place and provided ETA for canary and full rollout. Offered support to keep route override until full rollout completes.

Follow-ups: (1) Add automated integration test for batching with large-context payloads. (2) Update runbook to include batching bypass for dedicated pools handling >25k context tokens. (3) Postmortem to be written after stable rollout.
